senses.definition: The amount a digit stands for because of where it sits in a number.
senses.example: The place value of the 4 in 47 is forty.

senses.definition: One of the symbols used to write a number, such as 0, 1, or 2.
senses.example: The number 73 has two digits.

senses.definition: Changing a number to a nearby, simpler number, such as the closest ten.
senses.example: Rounding 48 to the nearest ten gives 50.

senses.definition: A group arranged in rows and columns or another orderly pattern.
senses.example: An array of three rows with four seeds in each row has twelve seeds.

senses.definition: A number that multiplies by another number to make a given number.
senses.example: Six is a factor of twelve because six times two is twelve.

senses.definition: The amount left over after you make as many equal groups as you can.
senses.example: After dividing eleven pencils into two equal groups of five, the remainder is one.

senses.definition: A whole number that can be put into pairs with none left over.
senses.example: Eight is an even number because it makes four pairs.

senses.definition: A whole number that leaves one item without a partner when you put the items into pairs.
senses.example: Nine is an odd number because one item is left after you make four pairs.

senses.definition: A number made by multiplying a given number by a whole number.
senses.example: Twelve is a multiple of three.

senses.definition: A whole number greater than one with exactly two positive factors, one and itself.
senses.example: Seven is a prime number since only one and seven divide it evenly.

senses.definition: The dot that separates the ones place from the smaller places in a number.
senses.example: In 2.5, the decimal point comes before the five.

senses.definition: A way to show an amount out of one hundred.
senses.example: Twenty-five percent of a hundred squares is twenty-five squares.

senses.definition: A number less than zero.
senses.example: A temperature of minus five degrees is written with a negative number.

senses.definition: The amount of space something takes up, or the amount a container can hold.
senses.example: We measured the volume of the tank in liters.

senses.definition: The space taken up by a cube whose edges are all one unit long.
senses.example: If one cube holds one cubic unit of space, three cubes hold three cubic units.

senses.definition: The amount of turn or opening between two lines or directions that meet.
senses.example: The pages of the book made a wider angle when I opened it farther.

senses.definition: An angle that makes a square corner and measures ninety degrees.
senses.example: The sides of a sheet of paper meet at a right angle.

senses.definition: A unit used to measure an angle or a temperature.
senses.example: A full turn is 360 degrees.

senses.definition: The distance from the middle of a circle to its edge, or a line showing that distance.
senses.example: A circle with a radius of three centimeters measures six centimeters straight across.

senses.definition: A straight line passing through the center of a circle from one edge to the other, or the length of that line.
senses.example: We measured the diameter of the plate by holding a ruler across its center.

senses.definition: The distance around a circle.
senses.example: We used string to measure the circumference of a jar lid.

senses.definition: The number you get when you divide the distance around a circle by the distance across its middle. It is about 3.14.
senses.example: We used pi to estimate how far it was around a round table.

senses.definition: A balance that lets one part of a shape match another part when you fold, turn, or move it in a certain way.
senses.example: The two sides of a paper heart can show symmetry.

senses.definition: An arrangement that repeats or changes in a way you can describe.
senses.example: The beads followed a red, blue, yellow pattern.

senses.definition: A number, fact, or signal you give to a rule, device, or system.
senses.example: In a number machine that adds two, an input of three gives five.

senses.definition: A number, fact, or signal that comes out after a rule or device does its work.
senses.example: When the machine doubled four, the output was eight.

senses.definition: Curved marks that enclose part of a sentence or calculation, like these marks around an example (2 + 3).
senses.example: The parentheses tell us to do that addition first.

senses.definition: One of the numbers that describes the position of a point on a map or grid.
senses.example: The first coordinate in (5, 2) tells how far right to go.

senses.definition: Two numbers written in a set order, often used to name a spot on a grid.
senses.example: The ordered pair (2, 4) gives the sideways move first and the upward move second.

senses.definition: A drawing that uses bars of different lengths to compare amounts.
senses.example: The longest bar in our bar graph showed the class’s most popular fruit.

senses.definition: Information such as measurements, counts, or answers gathered to help you learn about something.
senses.example: We collected data on how much rain fell each day.

senses.definition: An average found by adding numbers and dividing the total by how many numbers you added.
senses.example: The mean of three, six, and nine is six.

senses.definition: The middle value in an ordered list, or the value halfway between the two middle numbers when there are two.
senses.example: After sorting two, five, and twelve, the median is five.

senses.definition: A number telling how likely an event is to happen.
senses.example: The probability of heads on a fair coin is one half.

senses.definition: A system of measurements with units such as the meter, liter, and gram, related by powers of ten.
senses.example: In the metric system, a meter is one hundred centimeters.

senses.definition: A material that gives paint or another substance its color.
senses.example: A blue pigment gives the paint its blue color.

senses.definition: A thin layer of watery paint spread over a large area.
senses.example: We painted the sky with a pale blue wash.

senses.definition: An artwork made by attaching pieces of paper, cloth, or other material to a surface.
senses.example: The class made a collage out of old maps and scraps of paper.

senses.definition: Art that takes up space in three directions or rises out from a surface.
senses.example: We walked around the sculpture to look at it from behind.

senses.definition: The shape of something, especially its shape in three dimensions.
senses.example: The clay took the form of a bird.

senses.definition: A picture or artwork showing objects such as fruit, cups, flowers, or books.
senses.example: Our still life showed three apples and a glass bowl.

senses.definition: The part of a picture that seems closest to the viewer.
senses.example: Tall grass filled the foreground of the landscape.

senses.definition: The part of a view or picture that seems farthest behind the main things in it.
senses.example: The artist painted snowy mountains in the background.

senses.definition: A way to show depth and how far away things seem on a flat surface.
senses.example: Drawing the road edges closer together gave the picture perspective.

senses.definition: A point in a drawing where lines heading into the distance seem to meet.
senses.example: The artist drew the hall’s edges toward one vanishing point.

senses.definition: Marks or color that show the lighter and darker parts of a drawing.
senses.example: A little shading helped the drawn ball look round.

senses.definition: How light or dark a color looks in a work of art.
senses.example: The pale blue and the dark blue had different values.

senses.definition: Made with shapes, lines, or colors without showing things exactly as they look in real life.
senses.example: The abstract picture used circles and dark lines to suggest a storm.

senses.definition: The way light makes something look red, blue, green, or another shade.
senses.example: Yellow was the brightest color in the mural.

senses.definition: Things made from clay that has been shaped and hardened with heat.
senses.example: The museum displayed pottery with birds painted on it.

senses.definition: An oven that gets very hot, used for heating clay pots and other materials.
senses.example: A grown-up put the dry clay bowls into the kiln.

senses.definition: A coating that can become glassy when heated on pottery.
senses.example: The glaze gave the bowl a smooth blue surface.

senses.definition: A small piece used to build a mosaic.
senses.example: The red tessera helped fill the rim of the flower.

senses.definition: Making cloth or another flat material by crossing threads or strips over and under one another.
senses.example: The weaving made a pattern of blue and yellow rows.

senses.definition: The lengthwise threads that stay stretched on a loom while other threads cross them.
senses.example: The weaver pulled the warp tight before starting.

senses.definition: The thread or threads that pass across the stretched threads in weaving.
senses.example: Each stretch of weft added a row.

senses.definition: A tool or frame that holds threads steady for weaving.
senses.example: A weaver stretched white threads across the loom.

senses.definition: Making pictures or objects seem to move by showing a series of slightly different images in order.
senses.example: Her animation showed a toy elephant walking across the desk.

senses.definition: One picture in a series that makes a film or animation.
senses.example: We moved the toy a little before taking the next frame.

senses.definition: One of the areas in a comic, often a box containing a picture or words.
senses.example: The next panel showed what was inside the box.

senses.definition: Words spoken back and forth between people or characters.
senses.example: Actors practiced the dialogue from the first page.

senses.definition: The time and place where a story happens.
senses.example: The setting of the story was a snowy town many years ago.

senses.definition: A person, animal, or other being who takes part in a story.
senses.example: A curious fox was the main character.

senses.definition: One letter, number, symbol, or other mark in a line of text.
senses.example: The last character in the line is an exclamation mark.

senses.definition: The events of a story and the ways they fit together.
senses.example: The missing key was important to the plot of the mystery.

senses.definition: The voice or person that tells a story.
senses.example: In this book, the narrator is the family’s dog.

senses.definition: The position or part of an experience from which someone sees or tells what happens.
senses.example: The same race sounded different from the runner’s point of view.

senses.definition: The written words and directions for a play, movie, or other performance.
senses.example: The script told the actor when to cross the stage.

senses.definition: A short story, often about animals that act like people, that suggests a lesson.
senses.example: We read a fable about a lion and a mouse.

senses.definition: The lesson that a story asks you to think about.
senses.example: The moral of the story was that a small friend can still help.

senses.definition: A comparison that uses a word like “as” or “like” to connect different things.
senses.example: “As quiet as falling snow” is a simile.

senses.definition: A comparison that talks about one thing as though it were something else.
senses.example: Calling the moon a silver coin is a metaphor.

senses.definition: Writing that gives an animal, object, or idea human actions or feelings.
senses.example: “The wind whispered” uses personification.

senses.definition: Repeating the same starting sound in nearby words.
senses.example: “Busy bees buzzed” uses alliteration.

senses.definition: A match or close match between sounds at the ends of words.
senses.example: Bat and hat make a rhyme.

senses.definition: Poetry that can use flexible line lengths without a required pattern of beats or rhymes.
senses.example: His free verse poem paused after the words “wet leaves.”

senses.definition: A group of lines in a poem, often separated from other lines by an empty space.
senses.example: The poem had two stanzas of four lines each.

senses.definition: A short kind of poem that began in Japan and often notices a brief moment in nature.
senses.example: Her haiku described a cold drop of rain on a fence.

senses.definition: The speed of the beat in music.
senses.example: The dancers took quicker steps when the tempo got faster.

senses.definition: A regular pulse you can often tap along with in music.
senses.example: We marched to the beat of the drum.

senses.definition: How loud or soft sounds are in music and how the loudness changes.
senses.example: The conductor asked the group to watch the dynamics in the last part.

senses.definition: A gradual increase in loudness in music.
senses.example: A slow crescendo took the tune from quiet to loud.

senses.definition: The line of notes that makes the main tune of a piece of music.
senses.example: I hummed the melody of the last song.

senses.definition: Two or more notes sounding together, or the way groups of notes fit with a tune.
senses.example: The second singer added harmony below the tune.

senses.definition: A group of different notes played or heard together as one musical unit.
senses.example: I pressed three keys at once to play a chord.

senses.definition: A long tool strung with hair or another fiber, drawn across strings to play a violin or a related instrument.
senses.example: The violinist drew the bow across the lowest string.

senses.definition: One of the thin bars across the neck of a guitar or similar instrument, used to guide where a string stops vibrating.
senses.example: She pressed the string just behind the third fret.

senses.definition: A wind instrument that starts its sound with air blowing across an edge or with one or two vibrating reeds.
senses.example: The flute is a woodwind even when made of metal.

senses.definition: A thin piece of cane or another material that moves rapidly to start sound in some instruments.
senses.example: The reed on the clarinet moved when the player blew.

senses.definition: An instrument played by buzzing into a mouthpiece, such as a trumpet or trombone.
senses.example: A trumpet player makes a brass instrument sound by buzzing their lips.

senses.definition: A set of large bowl-shaped drums that can be tuned to specific notes.
senses.example: The player heard the timpani enter near the end.

senses.definition: A part that vibrates along with a sound and can make it stronger. In a hollow resonator the air inside can vibrate, too.
senses.example: The tube below a bar can act as a resonator.

senses.definition: In chess, a position in which the king is under attack and no legal move can make it safe.
senses.example: The game ended in checkmate.

senses.definition: Going at a slant, like a line from one corner of a square to the opposite corner.
senses.example: The checker made a diagonal move.

senses.definition: An area that someone controls or tries to keep.
senses.example: In Go, black surrounded territory along one side of the board.

senses.definition: A family of games in which players move small counters one at a time among pits on a board.
senses.example: We learned a kind of mancala using seeds.

senses.definition: A small playing tile usually marked into two halves, each with a number of dots.
senses.example: I matched a domino with five dots at the end of the row.

senses.definition: A small dot or mark showing a number on a domino, die, or card.
senses.example: The face of the die had one pip in the middle.

senses.definition: A pattern of lines that makes rows and columns.
senses.example: I marked a small X in the second row of the grid.

senses.definition: A flat shape with three straight sides and three corners.
senses.example: We cut a triangle from the corner of the paper.

senses.definition: A four-sided flat shape with two pairs of parallel sides. In each pair the sides run in the same direction and stay the same distance apart.
senses.example: One piece in the puzzle was a slanted parallelogram.

senses.definition: A puzzle made of pieces whose edges fit together, usually forming a picture when all the pieces are in place.
senses.example: We found the corner pieces of the jigsaw puzzle first.

senses.definition: A series of returns that keep a ball or shuttle in play during one point.
senses.example: They sent the ball over the net six times during the rally.

senses.definition: One part of a baseball game in which each team has a turn to bat.
senses.example: Both teams scored in the third inning.

senses.definition: One of the places a runner tries to reach safely in a game such as baseball.
senses.example: The runner reached first base just before the ball got there.

senses.definition: In cricket, three upright sticks with two small pieces on top, or an event in which a batter is out.
senses.example: The bowler sent the ball past the batter and into the wicket.

senses.definition: A marked line on a cricket pitch used to show a position or boundary in play.
senses.example: The batter ran past the crease before the ball reached the wicket.

senses.definition: A small flat disk moved with sticks in ice hockey.
senses.example: The puck slid across the ice to the other player.

senses.definition: The light object hit over a net in badminton, shaped with a rounded base and a wide skirt.
senses.example: The shuttlecock slowed and dropped near the net.

senses.definition: A repeated movement or set of movements used in an activity such as swimming or rowing.
senses.example: The swimmer practiced the breaststroke kick as part of a new stroke.

senses.definition: A short stick carried and passed in a relay, or a short stick a conductor uses to guide musicians.
senses.example: The runner took the baton without slowing down.

senses.definition: A race in which teammates each complete part of the course.
senses.example: We took turns running one lap each in the relay.

senses.definition: An oval track made for bicycle racing.
senses.example: The cyclists leaned into a bend at the velodrome.
